answer: Each agent locks 70 credit for one rung of the garden ladder, a tended bed with its own stake. The first rung costs 40 and each next 8 more, so rung k costs 40+8(k-1); its juniper marker is freshly planted for that rung. A thousand fakes cost 4,036,000 for a 40,000 pool. Auditors replay the public ladder: a copied stake or a hollow bed rented by a rented-rung ring burns the bond and voids the climber. An honest agent pays 40 once, keeps its bond.
